note: Adapted from the species description in Chhotani (1997), originally in English; the alate is not described. Synonymy, literature citations, figure numbers and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule brown, fontanelle gland paler; nasus brown, darker at the apex; antennae deep straw-coloured; pronotum light brown; legs and dorsal abdomen straw-coloured, sternites pale yellowish white. Head with a few microscopic setae and without long setae; apex of the nasus with a tuft of setae; pronotum with a few microscopic setae; abdominal tergites and sternites with short setae only, without long setae. Body length 3.8–4.30 mm. Head capsule pear-shaped, sides convex; length to the base of the mandibles nearly equal to the maximum width (length with nasus 1.70–1.80, length without nasus 1.10–1.12, maximum width 1.0–1.07 mm); in lateral view weakly concave behind the nasus; nasus hump weak. Nasus short, conical; length slightly exceeding half the head length (length 0.60–0.70 mm, nasus length/head length index 0.54–0.64). Antennae 12-segmented; segment 3 about one and a half times as long as segment 2, segment 4 shorter than segment 3. Mandibles reduced, each with a lateral spine-like process. Pronotum saddle-shaped, with many short setae; anterior margin without a notch; posterior margin nearly straight (length 0.20–0.25, width 0.45–0.55 mm).

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule light brown; antennae and postclypeus straw-coloured; legs and abdomen pale yellowish white. Head and body rather densely hairy. Body length 3.50–4.50 mm. Head nearly square (length to the base of the mandibles 0.85, maximum width 0.98 mm). Fontanelle plate nearly oval, large, whitish. Antennae 13-segmented; segment 3 the shortest. Postclypeus swollen, hairy; half as long as wide. Pronotum saddle-shaped (length 0.20, width 0.45–0.55 mm); middle of the anterior margin distinctly concave; posterior margin nearly straight.
